title: Catch, send, and survive signals
brief: Install handlers with signal.signal, send signals with os.kill, decode death-by-signal statuses, and build run_with_timeout with SIGALRM and SIGKILL.
hints: `signal.signal(signum, handler)` returns the previous handler. Keep it, and put it back in a `finally` block so your function leaves no trace.
`SIGKILL` and `SIGSTOP` cannot be caught. `signal.signal` raises `OSError` for them, which is all `can_catch` needs to notice.
To make signals pile up, block them first with `signal.pthread_sigmask(signal.SIG_BLOCK, {signum})`. They wait as pending, and unblocking delivers them. Pending standard signals do not queue.
A child that installs a handler races with a parent that sends the signal. Have the child write a byte to a pipe after `signal.signal`, and have the parent read that byte before it calls `os.kill`.
For `run_with_timeout`, start a timer with `signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, seconds)` and a SIGALRM handler that raises an exception. The exception breaks `os.waitpid` out of its wait.
After a timeout, send `SIGKILL` (a child can ignore `SIGTERM`), then call `os.waitpid` again to reap it. Always cancel the timer and restore the old SIGALRM handler in `finally`.
